title: Natsume Sōseki's birth chart
metaDescription: Natsume Sōseki's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.9° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds an opposition to Uranus at 1.0° — close enough to weld taste to disruption. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 19.9° into Aquarius — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 17.9° Aquarius, Venus was at 3.8° Capricorn, Mars was at 11.8° Cancer. Read together: thought that travels by comparison; attraction that grows by reliability; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus opposition Uranus, 1.0° of separation. The scheme reads an opposition as an axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Mars square Neptune at 1.0°, and Mars sextile Pluto at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. The Sun in Aquarius at 19.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Cancer at 11.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements air 3, water 3, fire 2, earth 2; modalities fixed 5, cardinal 5. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Mars and Uranus were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.5° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 12.2°.
